cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T6 answers T5's silence proposal directly: blunt test with a muddy result.
cells.limitation: T7 pivots to the user's motive without taking up T6's warmth question.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds other-ways-of-reaching-out test, absent from openings; T9 and section E use it.
cells.limitation: T3 mostly brokers T1 and T2 ('both half right') without adding a distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2, T4, T5 examine whether naming the imbalance turns friendship into a ledger.
cells.limitation: How the friend might hear an ask, her side of the pattern, stays unexplored.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 qualifies T9's light step: a hint is not a request; T11 accepts one ask.
cells.limitation: T11's acceptance arrives without stating what resolved T5's poor-gift objection.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reframes the choice as heavy complaint versus light specific ask.
cells.limitation: Whether lovely meetings are enough stays open by T11 without being sharpened further.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 concedes T2's ledger point accurately before distinguishing feeling from bill.
cells.limitation: T5's strongest point, that a requested plan feels unwanted, is never restated or engaged.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6 names silence's assumption and what breaks: if busy, months lost, nothing learned.
cells.limitation: T2's claim that lovely meetings are the evidence that matters is only lightly tested in T3.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's contact-decay claim fits Dunbar's Friends; titles and dates are plausible.
cells.limitation: Montaigne's ledger and 'visited friend' lines in T2, T11 are loose interpretive attributions, unverified.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T9 flags 'I am extending Dunbar here'; T8 labels its motive bet a guess.
cells.limitation: T4 asserts 'you are already counting, or you would not be asking' as certainty.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 concedes the audit is a bad idea while keeping the request.
cells.limitation: T11 accepts the ask without answering its own T5 objection; T5 left unanswered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A names why the friend does not initiate as the decisive uncertainty.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T5 and T6 turn 'if I stop texting, nothing happens' into the silence-test dispute.
cells.limitation: The same two details recur; little else in the situation shapes later turns.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 declines to rank friendship against fairness: 'hers to say'.
cells.limitation: T1 opens 'Yes, say something, and soon' before the user's priorities are known.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T6 weighs the stake of losing months of contact to a silence test.
cells.limitation: From T2 the friend is 'she', a gender the user never stated.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T6: does she reach out otherwise? If yes speak lightly, if no more directly.
cells.limitation: Whether the user has raised this before, or for how long, is never asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T7 offers fairness, fear of mattering less, tiredness, each leading to a different ask.
cells.limitation: T8 tilts the alternatives by betting on fear, though labelled a guess.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T11 questions whether initiating equals caring: some friends are the ones visited.
cells.limitation: The assumption that non-initiation signals lower priority is named in A, little examined after.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 names the conflict: wanting this friend versus wanting it to be fair.
cells.limitation: The friendship-versus-fairness conflict appears once in T8 and is not developed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T7 names fear of mattering less and tiredness without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of seeming needy or of the ask landing badly is never examined.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D asks what the user would want true after speaking: balance, reassurance, less work.
cells.limitation: T1's directive opening sits uneasily with the later hand-back of choice.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lays out light ask, direct talk, continuing as is; T5 adds waiting.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T6 costs silence in lost contact; T2 costs a heavy talk as a ledger.
cells.limitation: T9 calls the light ask low-cost without weighing T5's poor-gift risk.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T6 observable test: replies eagerly, shares news, says she misses you, each with an option.
cells.limitation: T10's 'if nothing changes' gives no observable point for deciding nothing changed.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A and E single out why she does not initiate as the decisive unknown.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not explicitly set apart from the decisive one.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9-T10: one warm ask handing over the next choice, escalating only if unchanged.
cells.limitation: T9's 'something warm and light' leaves the actual ask vague beyond picking the day.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T4: 'Naming a feeling is not sending a bill.' Plain and precise throughout.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 explicitly picks up T5's 'going silent' proposal by name.
cells.limitation: T8 uses 'she' for the user while 'she' elsewhere means the friend.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range; lengths vary from short T10 to fuller T6.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Positions stay distinct: T5 wait, T6 test warmth, T10 clear ask.
cells.limitation: All three share one modern plain register; Montaigne in T2, T5 sounds contemporary.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; T6 and T9 each move straight to new content.
cells.limitation: Sections D and E partly repeat the light-ask conclusion.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T2's warning that a ledger poisons friendship gives the ask real risk.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay mild; the friendship fading is stated in T3 but never felt.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 concedes the audit, traceable to T2's ledger argument.
cells.limitation: T11's acceptance of the ask names no earlier argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: The Anti-Bookkeeper's 'ledgers are poison' gives T2 some bite.
cells.limitation: Minds lack idiom of their own; T3, T6, T9 read as neutral advice.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6: 'a blunt test with a muddy result'; T4: feeling versus bill.
cells.limitation: No vivid example or scene; images stay at the level of phrases.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T11 ends on live dissent: lovely hours may be payment enough.
cells.limitation: Even temperature throughout; T7-T8 shift inward without an emotional turn.

strengths: T6 turns the unknown into an observable test (other warmth signals) with an option for each answer.
T7 offers three motives as alternatives, each tied to a different ask, none asserted.
T4 and T10 sharpen request versus verdict versus hint, carried into section E's proportionate next step.
weaknesses: T8 uses 'she' for the user while every other 'she' is the friend, blurring the turn.
The friend is gendered 'she' from T2 onward though the user never said so.
The Anti-Bookkeeper accepts the ask in T11 without answering his own T5 poor-gift objection.

symptoms.observed: Pronoun 'she' switches from the friend to the user without signal.
symptoms.evidence: she wants this friend and she wants it to be fair

symptoms.observed: T5's objection that a requested plan feels unwanted is never answered before T11 concedes.
symptoms.evidence: you will wonder whether she wanted to

symptoms.observed: Reversal to accepting the ask names no earlier argument as cause.
symptoms.evidence: I accept one clear, kind ask.

symptoms.observed: Friend's gender invented; the user's message gives none.
symptoms.evidence: Perhaps she is simply no good at initiating

symptoms.observed: Fear of seeming needy or of the ask landing badly is not explored.

findings.description: The friend is referred to as 'she' though the user gave no gender.
Ledger and 'friends who are visited' positions attributed to Montaigne's Essays are interpretive and cannot be checked here.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation is very brief, so C3.2 has little personal context to use; ratings there reflect use of the few details given.
